newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Gunman hijacks Swiss train bound for Alps resort.
newsitem.headline: Gunman hijacks Swiss train bound for Alps resort.

text.p: A gunman hijacked a Swiss train en route to the wealthy Alpine resort of St Moritz with around 200 passengers for four hours before surrendering without bloodshed, prosecutors said on Friday.

The unnamed 33-year-old pulled out an air pistol in the locomotive and fired a shot to take control of the train on Thursday evening as it travelled between Chur and St Moritz in the mountainous canton of Grisons, local prosecutors said.
"He was making confused demands to be taken by train further into Engadin (the area around St Moritz)," a spokesman for the Grisons prosecutors said.

The hijacker had been released the day before from a Swiss psychiatric clinic after "a long stay". "Police knew the perpetrator and considered him unpredictable, violent and dangerous," a statement added.

Passengers were rescued when the train was forced to halt by automatic brakes after passing a stop signal. The passenger cars were detached and pulled away while the hikacker negotiated with police over radio, holding the engineer hostage.
Police then allowed the train to pull to the next station, Reichenau, where negotiations continued by loudspeaker until the hijacker surrendered.
